Interesting. I know very little about this topic, but as I read my thoughts immediately went to the evolutionary biologist Robert Sapolsky and his book The Trouble With Testosterone. I would encourage you to go down that pathway and add it into your thinking. I’m curious what the Bolt people would say to these arguments.

It has been some time since I read the book so I got some LLM summaries to refresh me on why many evolutionary biologist consider testosterone an expensive biological tax. I’m going to paste some of it here:

In the wild, maintaining high testosterone levels is akin to driving a car with the engine red-lining. It provides short-term power for mating and fighting, but it wears down the machinery (the body) much faster. Here is a breakdown of the specific evolutionary costs Sapolsky and other biologists highlight, focusing on the immune system and metabolic “taxes.” 1. The Immunocompetence Handicap This is the central theory explaining why high testosterone is costly. The “Handicap Principle” suggests that because testosterone suppresses the immune system, only males with superior genetics can afford to maintain high levels of it. The Trade-off: Energy is finite. The body must choose between investing in survival (immunity, cell repair) or reproduction (muscle mass, aggression, mating displays). Testosterone forces the body to prioritize reproduction at the expense of survival. The “Honest Signal”: High T features (like a peacock’s tail or a stag’s massive muscles) are “honest signals” to females because they are dangerous to possess. The male is essentially saying, “Look at how strong my genes are—I can handicap my own immune system with this much testosterone and still be standing.” Parasitic Load: In wild primate studies, males with the highest testosterone often have the highest burden of intestinal parasites. Their immune systems are less efficient at fighting off low-level infections because their energy is diverted elsewhere. 2. Metabolic & Physiological Costs Beyond just the immune system, high testosterone extracts a heavy toll on the body’s daily maintenance. Metabolic Burn: Testosterone is metabolically expensive. It forces the body to build and maintain lean muscle mass which burns calories at a much higher rate than fat. In a food-scarce environment (which is most of evolutionary history), having high T is a risk; you are more likely to starve during a famine. The “Good Cholesterol” Crash: Testosterone generally lowers HDL (good cholesterol). Sapolsky notes that this is one reason why males across many species die younger than females. The hormone that helps you win the fight today clogs your arteries for tomorrow. 3. Behavioral “Taxes” High testosterone lowers the threshold for risk-taking, which carries a direct survival cost. Injury and Mortality: High-T males are more conspicuous and more likely to engage in risky confrontations. In the wild, “winning” a fight often leaves a victor injured, making them susceptible to infection (which their T-suppressed immune system is now less equipped to fight). Parental Investment: Evolutionarily, there is often an inverse relationship between testosterone and parental care. High T drives mating effort (seeking new partners) rather than parenting effort (caring for offspring). In species where offspring need high investment, high T can actually be an evolutionary disadvantage if the offspring die from neglect. Summary of the Trap The “trouble” Sapolsky identifies is that while high testosterone might help a male pass on genes (by winning a mate), it actively works against his staying alive. The Irony: Pro-TRT (Testosterone Replacement Therapy) arguments often frame high T as the key to “health” and “vitality.” From an evolutionary standpoint, nature views high T as the exact opposite: a calculated health risk taken solely to reproduce before you die.

I hope this is good food for thought and discussion. Thanks for your years of great blogging MMM!

So here was my eventual realization: I’ve only got one life to live, and at age 51 my next ten years are an absolute gift where I still have the body of a teenager. But my energy and motivation were seriously compromising this opportunity. They were truly not normal for such an otherwise healthy person.

So I tried it out and I’m thrilled that it actually WORKED! I’m back to the me I want to be. Given the precious and fleeting nature of life, making the most of it is worth pretty much anything it takes.

TRT done right should *extend* my life expectancy… but even if it hypothetically shortened it: would you rather live 30 fantastic years or 40 tired, sad ones where you wish you had more energy?

Billy Markus on human behavior: “People are not rational. They are rationalizing. Once you understand this simple fact, all the oddest human behavior will suddenly make way more sense.”

Testosterone cypionate (most common, what MMM is using) and enanthate (another commonly used ester) have a half-life of around 10 days, meaning that 10 days after your dose about half of it will be left. After a few weeks of weekly dosing the levels stabilize (you can math this out using mg if you want). There’s zero reason to dose daily. I actually tested twice-weekly dosing vs weekly with blood testing and there was no difference in my levels. Weekly is more than fine and you won’t notice any fluctuations. It’s pretty common for people to dose every other week, but weekly is more than sufficient to maintain consistent levels.

Another thing to keep in mind is that many hormones are highly dependent on how much thyroid hormones you have. If they are low, they will be low too (e.g. if you have hypothyroidism). Low testosterone could also just be an expression of low thyroid hormones, so get those checked first.

The way to think about thyroid hormones is that they are the “gas pedal” of your metabolism. Higher levels, more energy and motivation. Lower levels, the opposite.

If you go to the doctor check for TSH (which is an indirect marker of thyroid hormone levels) AND T3, which is the active thyroid hormone (often not checked).

The smart garden uses an LED grow light and pre-seeded plant pods to give you a bountiful harvest of basil, peppers, rosemary, and more.

We'll never say no to another throw or blanket, especially if it's heated. Don't knock it until you've tried it, because the feeling of being under one after you just walked the dog in 10-degree weather, or after you just got back from a long day outside in the snow, is the best feeling in the world. Do you have a creative family member or someone who likes to doodle as a hobby? If so, they will appreciate this blank canvas they can draw on using just water. Here's how it works: dip the brush in water, draw whatever you want on the surface of this board, then watch it disappear over time as the water evaporates. We love a no-mess art activity.

You may not want your little niece or baby cousin playing with your expensive camera or iPhone, but if they show interest in documenting the sweet moments at family gatherings, get them their very own kid-friendly camera. Who doesn't love getting out of the shower or tub and being wrapped up in a toasty towel? Cozy Earth consistently tops our editors' lists for the best bamboo sheets (the brand's pajamas are so comfy, too), so if you know your family members would appreciate new bedding, this set makes the perfect gift. Whether they want this for themselves or their guest rooms, I know the bougie sheets will be a hit with the practical aunts and uncles."

When there are four or more schedules to juggle in a household, it can feel overwhelming, which is why we're big proponents of a digital calendar that keeps things organized. This one is extremely popular and one of the more stylish options available.

She has learned so much independence and confidence in her daily routine. One of my favorite features is the privacy mode picture. This doubles as a picture frame. We like to rotate our pictures. Family pictures, landscapes, kids' art. We love our heart display." Another person wrote, "The Hearth Display has been a game changer for keeping our family organized. The shared calendar, chore tracking, and reminders are easy to use and actually get used by everyone. The touchscreen looks great in our home and feels intuitive. We love Framebridge's selection of photo ornaments, and this is the type of gift that works for any family member who's putting up a tree. Buying smart home gadgets can add up, so if you want that peace of mind without racking up your credit card bill, get a Ring Doorbell.

<em>Heated Rivalry</em> Season 2: Everything We Know So Far

📅 2025-12-12  |  Read Source →

Good news has arrived for Heated Rivalry fans. The steamy HBO Max and Crave show, based on the six-book series Game Changers by Rachel Reid, is officially returning for a second season.

“Watching our show become an international phenomenon has been extraordinary,” series creator Jacob Tierney and executive producer Brendan Brady said in a statement. “We’re profoundly grateful to everyone that has been on this journey with us. Being renewed for a second season so early is a true honor, and we can’t wait to bring you even more of what you love.”

Yes, HBO Max announced the news in December 2025. The streamer posted a video on Instagram with series stars Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie opening up a gift box with a hockey puck that says “Heated Rivalry” on one side and “Season 2” on the other. The video is captioned, “The game’s not over. Season 2 of #HeatedRivalry is coming to HBO Max.”

Justin Stockman, vice president of content and programming at Bell Media, said in a statement: “Heated Rivalry represents the very best of what Canadian creators can deliver: rich characters, compelling drama, and a world audiences want to live in. The response has been extraordinary, and seeing the series now traveling internationally is an incredible milestone.”

While the exact season 2 plot is still under wraps, Storrie hinted that it’ll be based on Rachel Reid’s sixth Game Changers book, The Long Game. “Start reading The Long Game if you want to spoil it for yourselves,” he said.

The novel continues to follow hockey rivals-turned-lovers Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie), who are still keeping their romance a secret—10 years in. A decade of hiding is a challenge for them both, but going public could sabotage their careers. “It’s time for them to decide what’s most important—hockey or love,” the book’s synopsis reads.

The season 1 finale ended with Shane and Ilya confessing their love to one another at Shane’s cottage before being accidentally outed when Shane’s dad swings by for his phone charger. After an emotional afternoon with his parents, the two young men start figuring out how they can have a future together in Canada and perhaps even come out someday.

In an interview with Variety after the season 1 finale, showrunner Jacob Tierney commented on the episode, plans for season 2, and how the series leaned more into romance than sex toward the end.

“There’s quite a bit of sex in The Long Game,” said Tierney. “But I think it functions differently in the second book, and that’s just what I want to do. The journey of this show, no matter how long it goes on for, will always be centered around the relationship between Shane and Ilya. Sex will always be a big part of it, like it is with any romantic relationship. But it’s really about continuing that progress of what happens after that first blush of love, what happens after you decide you’re in love and how do you sustain it?”

He continued, “That’s a very adult question: ‘We love each other, and now what? Does that mean everything’s easy?’ No, it does not. There’s loads of challenges that get thrown Shane and Ilya’s way. Beyond what’s in the books, I really don’t have an agenda besides that I love this couple and I love these characters, and I want to just hang out with them more and watch them grow more and watch them become better for each other.”

He also said that Kip and Scott’s characters will be back since their story overlaps with Ilya and Shane’s throughout Reid’s books.

Tierney shared more information about season 2 at BookCon on April 18, 2026.

“Long Game is…so long and it’s so gamey, like eating venison,” Tierney told attendees. “It really is different, and the challenge, from an adaptation standpoint, is you’re in much more serious territory. There’s still lots of flirting, and there’s lots of sex, but it’s this kind of danger. This kind of ‘hotel room, adolescent sex’ stuff is largely gone.”

He also revealed characters from Reid’s novel Role Model would be part of the season: Ottawa Centaurs forward (and Ilya’s new teammate) Troy Barrett and the team’s social media manager, Harris Drover, who have their own love story in the book.

“It’s very ‘grumpy sunshine.’ It’s very ‘apple orchard,’” he said. “It can drift into things that you want, but Troy is a really damaged guy. And Troy is quite damaged on the show. I would say we’re digging into that even harder.”

Entertainment Weekly revealed the logline for season 2 that day: “The Long Game picks up 10 years into their relationship. Shane and Ilya’s love remains a secret, but Ilya has parted ways with his Boston team to play for the Ottawa Centaurs so that he can be closer to Shane. The pair have also launched their charity organization, which they spoke about at the famous cottage. While they are seeing each other more than ever, the potential price of going public with their romance weighs heavily on the couple, especially as Ilya wants them to come out of hiding much sooner than originally planned.”

Ilya’s friendship with Svetlana Vetrova (Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova) will also receive more attention in season 2.

Speaking at an October 2026 fan event in Brooklyn, Tierney explained that Svetlana gives Ilya someone to confide in, even when he isn’t being entirely truthful about his feelings.

“This happens a lot in season 2, where he’s lying, but at least he’s saying something out loud,” Tierney said, per E!. “It’s so interesting to have to watch him call her and be like, ‘I’m fine. I love it here.’ You’re like, ‘OK, well, you’re not.’”

On October 18, Kharlamova spoke to E! at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show about returning to set with the show’s growing ensemble. “It’s awesome,” she said of the new cast members. “It’s changed it for the better. It’s like having more friends there.”

Williams and Storrie will reprise their roles as Shane and Ilya, respectively, in Heated Rivalry season 2.

Crave and HBO Max revealed on August 7 that Justice Smith (Now You See Me: Now You Don’t) and Charlie Gillespie (One Night Only, Splitsville) will play the roles of Harris Drover and Troy Barrett, respectively.

“Rachel Reid has given us two beautifully layered characters in Harris and Troy who you can’t help but root for,” Tierney and Brady said in a joint statement. “From the start of the casting process, we knew we were looking for actors who could create something truly special together and bring that same depth and heart to the screen.”

“Justice and Charlie do exactly that,” they added. “They immediately connected with the vulnerability and resilience at the core of these characters, bringing an instinctive understanding of who Harris and Troy are.”

Justice’s casting led to some backlash from fans of the show, which he later addressed on Instagram.

“I have to say I am moved by the support and love I’m getting from fans in my dms, fans who have welcomed me with open arms and who already feel a responsibility to protect me,” he wrote in a text post shared to his Story. “I am honored to play a character that you all care about deeply and I promise that I will take good care of him if you give me the chance. I am beyond excited for the experience.”

Reid subtly addressed the drama on Instagram. “Thinking about all the people last summer who told me the casting for llya and Shane was wrong and bad…” she captioned an Instagram Story.

More casting announcements arrived on August 7. Deadline revealed that Emily Hampshire (Schitt’s Creek), Edvin Ryding (The Young Royals, 28 Years Later), Robert Naylor (Mile End Kicks), Sabrina Jalees (Black Mirror), and drag queen Priyanka (Drag Brunch Saved My Life, Meet Me Next Christmas) will be joining the cast for the next season.

According to the outlet, “Hampshire will play Vanessa, Ryding is Luca Haas, Jalees is Farah Jalali and Priyanka portrays Tarek.” Naylor, meanwhile, will play Wyatt Hayes in the series, a starting goaltender for the Ottawa Centaurs and a fan favorite character in the Game Changers book series.

Deadline reported on August 25 that Daniel Diemer and Shaheen Jafargholi will star in season 2 as Ryan Price and Fabian Salah. Ryan and Fabian are the leads of Reid’s Tough Guy, the third novel in the Game Changers book series.

“Fabian and Ryan each bring a distinctive energy to the world Rachel Reid has created,” Tierney and Brady said in a statement. “They are bold, complicated, and deeply compelling characters, and finding actors who could really take on all of those different sides was so important to us.”

The statement continued, “Daniel and Shaheen bring such confidence and emotional honesty to the roles. We can’t wait for audiences to see what they do with Fabian and Ryan and how they make these characters their own.”

Jafargholi shared the news of his casting to Instagram and captioned the post, “gag it.”

On September 1, Deadline reported that François Arnaud, Robbie G.K., Sophie Nélisse, Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova, Christina Chang, Dylan Walsh, Callan Potter, Benjamin Roy, and Kamilla Kowal would be returning for Heated Rivalry season 2.

Two days later, on September 3, Deadline reported three more additions to the season 2 cast. Kevin Zegers will play Coach Wiebe, Paul Gross will appear as Commissioner Roger Crowell, and Milla Jovovich will take on the role of Dr. Galina Molchalina.

On September 17, Deadline reported that six new cast members would be joining the cast of season 2. The Handmaid’s Tale alum Brendan Morgan will play Zane Boodram. Michelle Mylett (Letterkenny) will star as Lisa. Lauren Chan (The Devil Wears Prada 2) will play Gen. Other additions include Gerry Dee (Animal Control) as Coach Cooper and Nick Stahl (Terminator 3) as Curtis Barrett.

David Tomlinson (Fellow Travelers, Silent Night, Deadly Night) also joins the cast of season 2 and will play Cody Kent, which will be a name change of the character of Dallas Kent in the Game Changers book series.

The singer would like to. At the Palm Springs International Film Festival, she told Variety, “Oh, I’m so in [to do music]. Book me. Get me booked!”

A day later at the Critics Choice Awards, Variety asked Arnaud about Cyrus’s interest. “I think we might get a little bit bigger budget for season 2, but I don’t know if we get Miley budget,” he admitted, before adding, “I think if she sees the show, she might give us a discount.”

In a February 2026 interview with GQ, Williams spoke about his hopes for his character Shane’s growth in season 2. “I want to see what Shane looks like when he comes into himself and moves away from fear and stifling of his emotions,” he said.

Williams also reflected more broadly on how he chooses projects at this stage of his career. “It starts with the script, and comes down to the director/creator,” he said. “No actor can turn shit writing into something great. And at the end of the day, a subpar director can butcher a good performance—and even a good script if they’re really bad—by fumbling the movie at so many points along the way.”

In September 2026, Williams admitted that getting back into character was initially difficult for him and Storrie.

“He [Storrie] worked through day one. I worked day two of shooting,” he said during a TIFF Q&A. “And he came back—and I don’t think he’d mind if I said that—but he was like, ‘It was sort of weird. They were all so good that I was like am I good? Am I in it? Am I doing the thing? Am I doing like an impression of Ilya?’ And we were talking about this before we even started shooting. And I was like, it’s weird that our memory of playing season 1 isn’t just our true memory of showing up and doing the scenes. It’s having watched them cut together. It’s fan reactions. Our memory isn’t ours. It’s everyone’s, which is—it’s been abstracted and twisted, and it’s become this weird amalgamation of a memory.”

Williams went in confident that he could recapture Shane on his first day of shooting. That wasn’t what happened. He had been shooting with some extras who were fans. He suddenly thought to himself, “Oh god, oh god, am I doing a Shane expression? Okay, and I was like, Oh, I’m losing it, I’m losing it.”

He and Storrie compared their experiences and found it became much easier to play their roles in the days that followed.

“After our first day ones, it came back, thankfully, because Jacob does a really good job of making the set feel as tiny as it was in season 1,” he explained. “It’s all the same crew, which is really great. But it was surreal to step into it.”

Tierney and Brady spoke with Gayle King on CBS Mornings on Feb. 26, 2026, and said that the second season of Heated Rivalry is currently being written, with filming set to begin in August 2026.

“There will be more Heated Rivalry on your TVs, like, truly, as soon as humanly possible,” Tierney said. Brady added, “like the best parts of this show,” and that fans should “enjoy the yearn.”

On May 29, Tierney accepted the Showrunner Award at the third Critics Choice Celebration of LGBTQ+ Cinema & Television in Los Angeles via video, seemingly offering an update in his speech.

“Thank you so much to the Critics Choice Association for this amazing and unexpected honor,” said Tierney. “I’m so, so grateful, and I’m so sorry that I cannot be there to celebrate with all of you in person and accept this. I’m working very hard on season 2 to get it out to people as soon as possible. I genuinely wish I could be there. I’m so moved by this.”

Tierney also discussed season 2 during a BookCon panel in New York in April 2026, when he confirmed that Heated Rivalry is slated to return in spring 2027. He also shared more about his approach to adapting Reid’s The Long Game for the screen.

“I want to dig deeper,” Tierney said, per People. “Because everything in her book, there is the foundation of a very real and understandable queer relationship. And I didn’t want to shy away from it. I wanted to dig into it.”

There may be even more Heated Rivalry on the way. On November 7, Deadline reported that the series is filming its second and third seasons back-to-back, with both seasons expected to have six episodes. Production is reportedly slated to wrap in late November or early December.

According to Deadline, a standalone Heated Rivalry holiday movie is also in the works, with production expected to begin in December. The film is reportedly being planned for a theatrical release in December 2027 and will center on the series’ other season 1 couple, Scott Hunter (François Arnaud) and Kip Grady (Robbie G.K.). Additional characters from the show are also expected to appear, though the series’ central couple, Shane and Ilya, reportedly won’t be part of the film.

How to Watch the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade

📅 2025-11-18  |  Read Source →

As the turkey thaws and a day of cooking prep begins, an equally integral Thanksgiving tradition is Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. Last year, 3.5 million spectators lined New York City’s streets to watch the procession of vibrant balloons and whimsical floats bob and weave through Midtown Manhattan to the beats of countless marching bands and celebrity performers. Beyond the city, a record-setting 34.3 million tuned into the NBC and Peacock broadcast, making the Emmy-winning production the year’s most-watched entertainment telecast. This year's promises to be even grander, as 2026 marks the 100th anniversary of the spectacle, which started in 1924 (though it wasn’t held from 1942 to 1944 because parade materials were reserved for wartime efforts).

“As a kid from the Bronx, it is an honor to bring this cherished tradition…to the city of New York every year,” the parade’s executive producer since 2021 Will Coss tells Condé Nast Traveler. The annual highlight for him is seeing the joyful expressions of spectators of all ages as the parade passes them by “showcasing some of the most iconic and recognizable pop culture characters and figures.”

This year marks the 99th anniversary of the Macy's Parade, an annual Thanksgiving tradition.

On the eve of the parade's centennial, the team—composed of painters, carpenters, animators, sculptures, welders, designers, engineers, and electricians—is honoring its past by way of revived classics like Felix the Cat and Underdog balloons. Ardent fans will also find a swath of newcomers that include a Fantasia-inspired Mickey, cowboy Minion, and a Peanuts duo. “The team at Macy’s Studios works year-round to make this historic parade bigger and better for our audiences every year,” Coss says. Here’s everything you need to know about the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in 2026—all its surprises, delights, and familiar joys.

When Macy’s first debuted its one-million-square foot New York City flagship store at 34th Street between Broadway and Seventh Avenues in 1924, the retailer threw a Christmas parade on Thanksgiving morning to boost holiday sales—with a much longer route starting at 145 Street and Covent Avenue. Balloons joined the lineup in 1927, starting with Felix the Cat, and the festivities were first broadcast nationally in 1947.

These days, the festive parade follows a 2.5-mile path from the Upper East Side to Midtown Manhattan. Starting at the corner of 77th Street and Central Park West, the route heads south to Columbus Circle and then turns east, heading along 59th Street to Sixth Avenue. From there, it goes straight down Sixth Avenue to 34th Street, ending in front of Macy’s flagship store in Herald Square.

Clifford the Big Red Dog in Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

Coss recommends arriving early for a great view. Many spectators start to gather as early as 6 a.m. along the beginning of the route on Central Park West (approach from the west) from 61st to 75th Streets. Other prime spots include the south side of 59th Street between Columbus Circle and Sixth Avenue and the entire stretch of Sixth Avenue between 38th and 59th. Spectators should be aware there is no viewing on Central Park West between 59th and 60th Streets, or anywhere south of 38th Street.

Coss also reminds those bringing children to dress warmly for the chilly weather and to be prepared to entertain young ones for a few hours while waiting to spot the first float. He suggests avoiding strollers, large bags, backpacks, and umbrellas.

In celebration of its centennial, some 100 inflatables will fly. Returning after decades are much-anticipated Felix the Cat (the parade's first character balloon, introduced in 1927) and Blue Hippopotamus (from the 1931 parade), while Hello Kitty and Underdog (who appeared in every parade from 1965 through 1984) will also make cameos. New to the scene are Bluey, Buckaroo Bob the Minion, and Snoopy persona Joe Cool with Woodstock, among others. The procession will also welcome 52 floats, 31 clown crews, nine specialty units (such as trycaloons, or balloons ridden on tricycles), seven marching bands, and five balloonicles (that’s a balloon-vehicle hybrid).

TODAY’s Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb, and Al Roker will host the live broadcast of the 100th Macy’s Parade. Though this year's performance lineup has yet to be announced, the 2025 roster featured 26 celebrity performers, ranging from Colbie Caillat and Christopher Jackson to Foreigner and Taylor Momsen, complete with a performance by KPop Demon Hunters’ HUNTR/X singing voices EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami. As anticipation for the parade's centennial only increases, Coss says this year will “bring new surprises and delights to the iconic holiday tradition and truly celebrate this incredibly special anniversary.”

For some, the majestic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is an official marker of the transition into the Christmas season in New York City.

Americans can watch the live telecast on both NBC and Peacock on Thursday, November 26, from 8:30 a.m. to noon in all time zones, while Telemundo will air a Spanish-language simulcast hosted by Andrea Meza, Aleyda Ortiz, and Clovis Nienow. For late risers, an encore will air starting at 2 p.m. ET/PT, and the full broadcast will also be on NBC with live audio description on Secondary Audio Program channel (SAP). Behind-the-scenes footage will be shared on social media @macys and #MacysParade via Instagram, TikTok, and Threads.

To rev up for the turkey day excitement, “Countdown to the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade” will air on Wednesday, November 25, on NBC and Peacock. The primetime special will broadcast live from the parade starting line with exclusive previews and behind-the-scenes stories from the balloons and floats.

One of the most underrated—and free—ways to experience the parade is by attending the Thanksgiving Eve balloon inflating event on Wednesday, November 25, a “time-honored tradition and special peek into the parade celebrations,” Coss says. Since 1994, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade has invited guests to see the process the balloons undergo to reach their larger-than-life size and scale the afternoon before Thanksgiving. Last year’s took place between 1 p.m. and 6 p.m., with the line opening at noon.

Those interested can enter at West 72nd Street and Columbus Avenue, where they’ll be guided through a security checkpoint and then can roam between West 77th and 81st Streets to view the balloons. Note that prohibited items include bags or backpacks larger than 12-by-6-by-12 inches, lawn chairs, large coolers, alcoholic beverages, chairs, weapons, drones, pets, and umbrellas; participants will be screened before entering the route.

For the latest up-to-date information, visit macys.com/parade for details on the parade and nbc.com/macys-thanksgiving-day-parade for updates on the broadcast.

We Tested 15 Electric Mini-Inflators. These Tiny Pumps Are Fast Enough to Replace CO₂ on Many Rides

📅 2025-11-13  |  Read Source →

From 90-gram pocket pumps to premium inflators, these editor-tested picks make flat fixes easier.

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. How we test gear.

Pumping up tires is a constant of cycling. Whether you’re checking pressure before a road ride, fixing a mid-ride flat on your gravel bike, fine-tuning your air pressure at the trailhead, or topping up tires on your kid’s bike in the garage, every cyclist needs to put air in their bike’s tires

While some riders don’t worry about the exact psi in their tires, others constantly check and analyze their air pressure, and the latter group may be onto something. In his story, “More Speed and Comfort? The Right Tire Pressure Can Give You Both,” Test Editor Dan Chabanov explains that having the correct pressure in your tires provides more confidence and control on rides.

Small, portable electric inflators have recently taken the cycling world by storm and quickly gained popularity with riders. For several decades, traditional pumps (floor, frame, and mini), CO₂ cartridges, and air compressors have been the go-to methods for filling tires. While mini-inflators don’t fully replace these other inflator types, these small electric units are now finding their way into riders’ toolboxes, gear bags, jersey pockets, and seat bags.

Over the last two seasons, we’ve subjected 15 electric mini-inflators to the same tests. We originally tested 11 inflators in 2025. In November 2026, we tested 4 models (from Cyclami, PDW, State, and Lezyne) and updated our Best Mini-Inflators ranking. A handful stand out for specific use cases or rider types. But these are only a few of the great pumps out there; choose the one that best fits your needs and budget.

With svelte dimensions and a 106-gram weight, the Ultra Tiny is small enough to stash in a jersey pocket, flat kit, or bar bag. Plus, it quickly inflates tires of all sizes to pressure. The AS2’s super-accurate gauge also makes it worth considering for your home shop or carrying in a race-day tool kit. However, the pump runs a little hot.

At the media launch for the Colnago G-5X, someone asked the brand representatives if any inflators fit inside the internal frame storage. That led me to search for options that can fit inside frames. The Cyclami A5S came up in some discussions, so I ordered one on AliExpress to test.

Overall, it’s a solid little inflator that performs well—sub-one-minute inflation times and 122-gram weight. The rounded profile and placement of the air chuck (on top rather than the side) help it squeeze into many frames’ internal storage doors. Of the five road, gravel, and mountain frames in the office I checked, the A5S fit into four (it didn’t fit into the Cervélo Caledonia).

Several Bicycling editors rely on the Air Rush on rides and at home. Overall, it’s a solid and dependable pick. It has a nice display, runs cool, and inflates road and gravel tires in under a minute. It also filled five road tires; that’s better than most units. I only wish it were slightly smaller for carrying in a seat bag or internal frame storage.

Like many RockBros products, this mini-inflator isn’t the best at any single thing, but it does everything pretty well overall. It gets tires up to pressure in under 50 seconds, doesn’t run too hot, isn’t too loud, and isn’t super heavy.

The most expensive model in our test, the Ultimate, lived up to its name, hype, and steep price tag. And matching its durable appearance, this inflator is a beast—it gets tires up to pressure in under 30 seconds and inflates eight tires on a single charge. I tested Silca’s claim that the Ultimate will seat tubeless tires—surprisingly, it succeeded.

The Ultimate was the quietest inflator in our testing and tied for the second-lowest temperature. Other than price, the biggest negatives are the Ultimate’s weight and size. One note: after almost a year of frequent use, an O-ring inside the pump failed. However, Silca offered to replace the unit under warranty.

The Pocket SE doesn’t feature a display or gauge, but at only 90 grams, it weighs less than a single CO₂ cartridge and head. And though it takes roughly a minute to inflate a tire to full pressure, I can fill four tires on one charge. The Pocket SE’s one downside is that without a pressure gauge or a 72 psi cutoff, I’d be cautious using it on hookless tubeless road wheels.

For a year, I’ve carried the Pocket SE in my seat bag for flat fixes, and it has gotten me out of plenty of jams. My only complaint is that the button activates easily; a bump or pothole can trigger the unit if it isn’t carefully positioned in your bag.

Portland Design Works makes well-crafted, usable gear for everyday cyclists. The brand doesn’t take itself too seriously, and its products sometimes have whimsical or quirky elements (like its water bottle cages).

PDW’s Essentials inflator follows this mold—it’s well-designed, looks good, and functions well. The Essentials inflates tires quickly, and the gauge is pretty accurate. Its best feature is presets for different bike types (labeled road, gravel, mountain, and city). You can use these to set your tires for your quiver of bikes, or program them for different rides, wheelsets, or riders in your house.

The screw-on chuck is slightly tricky to use and leaks some air if not fastened correctly. While the unit’s body doesn’t run hot, the hose’s base certainly does: heed that yellow warning tag.

Mini-inflators are pint-sized electric air compressors. Larger electric pumps have been around for many years and are commonly used at home, in the garage, or the workshop. Some people carry electric pumps in their vehicles to air up car or truck tires and fill inflatable rafts or SUPs. Cordless air inflators have been a common sight around World Cup mountain bike team paddocks and cyclocross pit zones for several years.

Yet cyclists only started using these inflators within the last three years, when the prices dropped, the form factor shrank, and battery life increased. Riders soon found electric inflators perfect for the garage or the trailhead. Plus, their smaller size makes them much easier to toss in a bike bag or luggage than a floor pump when flying with a bike.

Several cycling equipment brands have released models tailored to bicycle riders’ tastes and preferences. Some companies have even cut enough weight and reduced the proportions to make electric mini-inflators a viable option for carrying in a jersey pocket or flat kit on rides.

The current crop of bike-specific mini-inflators can be broken down into two groups:

1) Small enough to bring on a ride, and 2) Everything else.

Of course, your definition of “small enough” might vary greatly from another cyclist’s. If you ride with a bar bag or frame pack, an inflator like the Portland Design Works Essentials or Trek Air Rush might be sufficiently tiny. However, if you carry everything in a ride wallet or obsess about weight, even Silca’s 112-gram Elettrico Micro might be too large for you.

For our testing, we focused on mini-inflators sold by cycling-specific brands and ones marketed for bicycle use. This isn’t an exhaustive test of every inflator available; instead, it provides context to help you choose one best for your needs.

In two years of testing, we’ve evaluated fifteen models across a wide price range ($15 to $160). These include mini-inflators from respected cycling brands, options from smaller companies, and those that fly under the radar.

To test if size matters, I picked some based on their tidy proportions and low weight. I also chose a couple of larger, heavier options to see whether they push air significantly faster or fill more tires than other mini-inflators. I also bought the cheapest mini-inflator available on Amazon ($14.90 on the day I was shopping) to test it against the pack and see if spending more on a pump really matters.

As with other Bicycling head-to-head product tests (like insulated water bottles, flared handlebars, and wide road tires), we evaluated electric mini-inflators based on real-world requirements, not intricate lab tests. Riders can replicate at home without much fancy equipment.

We inflated the tires to air pressures for a 180-pound cyclist riding a road, gravel, and mountain bike in average conditions (as recommended by Wolf Tooth’s app). For road riders, we recorded the time to inflate a 28mm-wide tubeless tire to 65 psi. We also measured the time to reach 30 psi on a 45mm gravel tire. For mountain bike riders (or folks riding new-school gravel bikes), we clocked the time to 20 psi on a 29x2.3-inch tire. To evaluate the pumps without built-in gauges, we measured the pressure they reached after 50 seconds.

After timing inflation speeds for each category, I fully recharged all devices. The next morning, I tested how many times each electric mini-inflator could fill a 28mm road tire to 65 psi from fully flat. To prevent overheating, I let each inflator cool down for ten minutes between fills.

In addition to real-world tests, we also measured three common concerns of electric pump buyers: Temperature, noise, and gauge accuracy. For these tests, I borrowed equipment from my colleagues on the Popular Mechanics test team.

This included a specially designed fixture that measures bike pump gauge accuracy. Gauge accuracy is important, especially for riders using hookless tubeless road wheels. Since the maximum allowed pressure for these wheel systems under ETRTO standards is 5 bar (72.5 psi), you don’t want to risk a tire blowing off a rim due to a wildly inaccurate pump reading.

Like other users, I have personally experienced noise and heat build-up issues with electric mini-inflators. Early one morning at Sea Otter Classic, my inflator woke the cyclist in the hotel room next door—my sincere apologies to him! Later, on an All Bodies on Bikes group ride, the inflator I borrowed from another cyclist to change a flat melted the plastic valve of my spare TPU tube.

Lesson Learned: Due to excess heat, always use an extension hose when filling plastic-valved tubes with an electric mini-pump.

“Do I plan to carry this on rides?” you ask when purchasing a mini-inflator. If you answered “yes”, look for lighter-weight and smaller-profile models. If you only plan to use the inflator at home, at the trailhead, or at races, don’t focus on size or weight.

Unless you only need to get out of a jam on the side of a road or trail, look for models that fill more than two tires. This allows you to adjust tire pressure and inflate tires on other bikes or spare wheels (and for friends to borrow before a ride—because you know they will need it).

After evaluating these mini-inflators, my key takeaway is that price doesn’t exactly make it the best for your needs. The most expensive pump in our test has brilliant inflation speed, is the quietest, and doesn’t run hot—plus it fills lots of tires. But it’s too heavy and large for most cyclists to carry on rides. However, spending more doesn’t guarantee better performance either, as some pricier models didn’t outshine the low- or mid-priced models. And, as I found out from testing, you probably don’t want to buy the absolute cheapest possible option either (luckily, this model is no longer available).

Skimming listings for different devices, you’ll notice (from similar design details and parts) that a select few vendors manufacture many electric inflator models for every brand. But even if a mini-inflator shares the same outer silicone protector, case, buttons, or display, it doesn’t mean they’re identical. For example, in our testing, the Rockbros model outperformed the extremely similar-looking Muc-Off Air Mach pump.

Unless you specifically need a lightweight, compact mini-inflator for on-the-bike use, spend a little more for a model with a built-in gauge. A display is super handy, and you can pre-set your desired pressure within 1 psi (some even read to tenths).

Pro Tip: If you buy an inflator without a built-in gauge, time how long it takes to reach your optimal ride pressure from fully flat before bringing it out on the road or trail. Then, when you’re airing up a flat fix, you can count off (or use a timer) to get you relatively close to your riding pressure.

As Deputy Editor, Tara Seplavy leads Bicycling’s product test team; after having previously led product development and sourcing for multiple bike brands, run World Championship winning mountain bike teams, wrenched at renowned bicycle shops in Brooklyn, raced everything from criteriums to downhill, and ridden bikes on six different continents (landing herself in hospital emergency rooms in four countries and counting). Based in Easton, Pennsylvania, Tara spends tons of time on the road and trail testing products. A familiar face at cyclocross races, crits, and bike parks in the Mid Atlantic and New England, on weekends she can often be found racing for the New York City-based CRCA/KruisCX team. When not riding a bike, or talking about them, Tara listens to a lot of ska, punk, and emo music, and consumes too much social media.

I take my holiday gift shopping very seriously — if not for my giftee, for my own serotonin-seeking purposes. There’s nothing quite as satisfying as finding the right N/A cocktail bundle for your aunt, or a cake stand that doubles as a chip and dip bowl (the in-laws will love that one) for the avid entertainer.

We’re all on different budgets; some are on the hunt for tasty bargains and piggy-bank-friendly stocking stuffers, while others have a more robust chunk of change set aside for providing big-impact presents You might have already bookmarked Eater’s gift guides that are under-$25, which is full of all kinds of chic home and kitchen goods, but now [turns up gas] we’re shopping at the under-$100 range, which gives us even more wiggle room to sweep your giftees off their feet via a ham-themed ornament, a robust at-home chai kit, or a set of steak knives from Peter Luger.

We’re in prime gift guide season, folks. Fasten your aprons, and let’s shop for every kind of food-loving person on your holiday list.

No cocktail has been living, laughing, and loving harder than the ultra-dirty martini lately. This briny bundle from Big Night brings together the shoppy shop’s sleek olive-themed hors d’oeuvres picks with a jar of Quincy’s big, juicy Castelvetrano olives, Quincy cocktail onions, and bag of Filthy’s cult-fave olive brine.

For my money, a solid indicator of a fun household is whether or not there’s a wild cheese or cutting board in the mix. This psychedelic slab from Fredericks and Mae is both a beautiful serving board and functional chopping block for all of your kitchen needs, because it’s made out of a durable and non-toxic HDPE material.

Fredericks and Mae Red/Blue Cutting Board

The organic Los Angeles lifestyle brand Flamingo Estate has created the pasta-lover’s dream present: a chic trio of pomodoro rosso sauce, angel trumpet pasta, and a bottle of Flamingo Estate’s heritage EVOO. As with the rest of the Estate’s bundles, this set comes housed in one of its signature, ornate green boxes.

Imagine the flex of sawing through a Porterhouse at home with Peter Luger logo-stamped blades, which are made with stainless steel and wood handles that will transport their giftee back to the hallowed halls of the world-famous Brooklyn steakhouse. If you have a bit more room left in your gift budget, I suggest pairing it with some New York strip steaks from Snake River Farms.

Diaspora Spice Co. is one of Eater’s favorite places to buy spices online, because it’s home to dozens of single-origin heirloom spices from (mostly) India and Sri Lanka. As founder Sana Javeri Kadri explains on its site, a core tenant of Diaspora Spice Co.’s operations is rooted in undoing colonialist inequity in the spice trade; in her words: “We’re proud to pay our farm partners an average of 6x above the commodity price. In a system where fair trade is a mere 15 percent premium, we pay what we believe to be a living wage.” The equitable spice brand has partnered with the North Carolina-based pottery and lifestyle brand East Fork on this at-home chai bundle, which features the former’s brand new masala chai blend, Madhur jaggery, a stainless steel strainer, and a panna cotta colorway kuhlad from the indie pottery company.

Eater’s deputy brand director Nat Belkov introduced me to Craighill, a company that reimagines everyday carry and home essentials (think, scissors and carabiners) with a little more design flair. The Brooklyn-based studio redesigned the common wine key, and Belkov tells me that it mitigates all the annoying little things that can go wrong while using a wine opener. “I love the perfect angle on the foil cutter,” he says, “[and] I love that they tapped the knowledge of sommelier André Hueston Mack to make sure it worked well enough to be trusted by members of the industry. Seldom do I run into a product where I genuinely have a hard time choosing between different color variations like here, with the sleek matte black, pop of orange, or classy tortoise finish. But most of all, I love that this thing is guaranteed to work for life.”

MoMA Design Store Bodum Neon Nesting Mixing Bowls (Set of 4)

As a person who drinks coffee every day (and feels horrified when I run out), I would be thrilled to receive this American Girl doll-sized bag (weighing 4 pounds) of beans from the award-winning Joshua Tree Coffee. This year, the Big Bag — which is filled with the beans of your choice — even comes with a cute enamel mug.

Joshua Tree Coffee Big Bag & Bellied Enamel Mug Bundle

The Chitose is kind of like the Ferrari of kettles, because it boils water extremely fast and is made out of professional-grade, scratch-resistant 18-8 stainless steel. Plus, it cuts a cute silhouette and is compatible with induction top stoves.

Japanese Taste Chitose Induction Compatible Japanese Stainless Steel Kettle

These pastel eggnog petit fours come from the acclaimed Los Angeles-based confectionary Valerie Confections, and are made of a rich spiced buttercake, with bourbon ganache layers dipped in white chocolate and garnished with 23-karat gold leaf and chocolate biscuit pearls.

Ghia’s apéritif box is one of those drink-themed holiday gifts that sells out every year, because it pairs the brand’s signature amaro-esque N/A ambrosia with chic glassware from French-American glass artist and designer Sophie Lou Jacobsen. Whether you’re shopping for someone who doesn’t drink or is just trying to drink less alcohol in the new year, it’s a fashionable foot forward in the world of booze-free drinks.

Owning a double burner griddle is the culinary equivalent to flexing a California king size bed, because it can handle all of the pancakes, eggs, and grilled cheese orders from the family (without having to hop between skillets like a stove DJ). We love this one from Lodge, known for its excellent cast iron cookware.

Lodge Blacklock Triple Seasoned Cast Iron Double Burner Griddle

It’s likely that your giftee already owns cocktail glasses, but there’s also a non-zero chance that they’ve had a few stunners from their collection broken by jolly, wobbly party guests. Eater collaborated with heritage crystal glassware company Zwiesel Fortessa on a collection of timeless pieces, including this versatile set of six Nick and Nora-style glasses.

Eater x Zwiesel Fortessa Folly Crystal Glass, 6 Ounce Cocktail (Set of 6)

Sometimes the best present is one that contains even more presents: a giant box of Swedish candies, all curated by the cult-fave confectioners at BonBon. Dubbed the Holiday Connoisseur Box, this light pink coffret is filled with classic BonBon gummies (I spy Pippi Longstocking’s Gold Coins) and plenty of Swedish classics like Marabou Japp chocolate bars and Juleskum marshmallow candies.

Kudos to Emma Chamberlain on this postmodern-feeling French press. The YouTuber went viral yet again for her collaboration with West Elm, and this coffee press in particularly takes notes from its elders (Bodum and Alessi) with its sleek stainless steel design.

Emma Chamberlain x West Elm Stainless Steel Button French Press

John Derian is the Final Boss of curating swish food-themed holiday ornaments (I do also need this energy drink-themed ornament), so it’s hardly surprising that the New York-based designer plucked this boneless cooked ham ornament for this year’s batch of stunners.

6 Best Early Black Friday Bed Frame Deals for Hundreds Off (2026)

📅 2025-11-11  |  Read Source →

Black Friday may still be a few weeks away, but some of our favorite furniture retailers are already rolling out deals, giving us an incentive to upgrade our bedroom setups sooner rather than later. Early Black Friday sales are delivering discounts on the bed frames of your dreams, from plush upholstered designs to sleek platform beds and clever storage solutions that might finally give that extra pile of bedding in your closet a proper home. Considering how much a new bed can cost, we’re more than happy to get a head start on the holiday shopping season.

A bed frame does more than hold your mattress. As the focal point of your bedroom, it sets the tone for the rest of your space, so it’s worth choosing one that looks good and holds up over time. The best designs combine thoughtful craftsmanship, sturdy construction, and a little personality. Practical features like built-in storage or a padded headboard for late-night reading are an added bonus. Ahead, we’ve rounded up some of the best early Black Friday bed frame deals worth now, including AD-tested favorites, statement-making picks, and plenty of reasons to finally give yourself the gift of a bedroom refresh.

Not every bedroom has room for nightstands, so West Elm’s Midcentury Storage Headboard Platform bed pulls double duty. Its clean lines, warm wood finish, and minimal silhouette offer an updated interpretation of classic mid-century design, but the real draw is the headboard, which conceals shelving behind sliding doors. It’s a clever place to stash books, charges, and all those other bedside essentials that need a home. During West Elm’s early holiday promotions, you can snag the goes-with-almost-everything bed frame for $300 off its original price.

Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert tested the bed in her son’s bedroom, where limited floor space made adding another dresser or nightstand impractical. “The doors run on little tracks and are embedded with little magnets that give it smooth and soft closure,” she shared. “Inside, you have a cutout for any wires, and these are accessible to all storage options.” She also appreciated how the blonde wood finish complemented the room’s contemporary aesthetic. A caveat for taller sleepers: the low-profile platform may make getting in and out of bed a little less comfortable.

Castlery’s Dalton Storage Bed may very well be the key to keeping your bedroom clutter-free. Its understated silhouette conceals spacious under-bed storage, making good use of otherwise wasted square footage. And if light-colored upholstery stresses you out for fear of spills and stains, the Dalton’s removable and washable linen-blend cover should offer some peace of mind.

Castlery’s early holiday sale is currently offering up to 50% off selected items, with additional tiered savings of up to $950 depending on how much you spend. The early access sale gives you the chance to upgrade your bed frame and increase your storage space in one fell swoop.

If the bedroom of your dreams is oozing with personality, CB2’s Russell upholstered storage bed in dusty lilac velvet is a worthy addition. Its subtle sheen and dramatic shelter-style headboard pair with a generously padded frame for a bed that feels akin to a piece straight out of a luxury boutique hotel. A large drawer hidden in the footboard adds a practical touch without interrupting the bed’s elegant silhouette. After all, who says statement-making furniture can’t also be cleverly designed?

Alpert tested the Russell in her own bedroom and was immediately taken with its unusual color, which she likened to amethyst. “This bed is a gem,” she said. The substantial headboard creates a cozy nook for reading, and she found that the footboard glides out smoothly, with plenty of space for spare quilts and bedding. “Climbing into this bed makes me think that I am going on a sleepcation,” she shared.

Serena & Lily has a knack for making rooms feel like they’ve been plucked out of a beautifully appointed beach house, even when the nearest coastline is nowhere in sight. A nod to 17th-century bobbin furniture, the Webster Bed brings that same breezy sensibility into the bedroom with turned-wood detailing and an open, airy frame. The intricate spindlework lends the bed plenty of character, whether you dress it up with crisp white linens or colorful patterned bedding. For the full seaside treatment, style the rest of your bedroom with woven accents and natural textures. With Serena & Lily’s current sale offering 26% off, it’s a particularly tempting excuse to bring a little vacation energy home.

If your ideal bedroom leans more serene sanctuary than grand hotel suite, Article’s Tessu bed frame might be the perfect gift to yourself before the holidays hit. Its low-slung design and softly textured boucle upholstery offer a refreshing alternative to the towering headboards and ornate detailing. The foam-padded frame makes reading or working from the comfort of your bed more comfortable, and wooden slats eliminate the need for a box spring. Originally $1,199, it’s currently marked down to $799, making this cozy, Scandi-inspired piece even more appealing.

A little bit of Old Hollywood glamour meets modern-day luxury in the Siren Queen Bed, designed by actor Laura Harrier and interior designer Tiffany Howell for Crate and Barrel. Inspired by vintage furniture and richly layered interiors, the Siren brings a distinctly designer look to the bedroom without much additional decorating. Keep the surrounding furniture simple and let this modern take on the classic sleigh bed take center stage. Right now, Crate and Barrel is offering over $1,000 off this unique piece, plus 20% back in rewards.

14 Best Early Black Friday Rug Sales to Style Every Room (2026)

📅 2025-11-07  |  Read Source →

Rugs are one of those niche investment pieces that can cost a fortune but will have little to no resale value after your dog has done a number on it (guess which one) or dust and hair have built up a layer of filth on top. All of which is to say, if you’re going to invest in a rug, you might as well get a good deal. Dear readers, now is that time.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday is when all the rug brands converge to roll out their biggest markdowns of the year, with deals from retail giants like Amazon and popular rug-exclusive retailers like Ruggable that make the business of underfoot fabrics its specialty. Below, a list of some of our favorite early Black Friday rug deals (and their makers). We’re tempted to bring these rugs home ourselves since we’re already seeing some designer pieces up to 50% off.

Stay tuned for more news on Black Friday events; we’ll update this guide as more sales are announced.

Design Within Reach is a go-to for iconic modern furniture and decor from brands like Herman Miller and Fritz Hansen. Its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales are among the few opportunities each year to score investment pieces at more approachable prices. Ahead of this year’s event, you can take advantage of up to 50% off clearance items, up to 40% off markdowns, and up to 25% off Herman Miller products. In the current bargain bin, you’ll find rugs spanning the shape, color, and pattern spectrum (like these two numbers, one from Beni Rugs and another direct from the retailer itself).

Ruggable is one of our favorite destinations for durable and washable rugs, whether you’re shopping for outdoor rugs, kids rugs, or even a doormat for your entryway. The brand’s ongoing Last Chance Hosting Sale rug sale includes up to 40% off select styles, many of which you can throw in the washing machine. Shameless plug: Our AD rug collection is also featured in the sale, including this Hema Persad design inspired by Moroccan textiles and architecture. “It fits perfectly in my space and was super easy to set up—the velcro underlay is game changing since I have an energetic puppy at home and it really holds the rug in place, even when she’s being rough with it,” says Stefanie Lindenbaum, director of project management and activation at Condé Nast, who tested out the rug. She also found it easy to clean after a puppy accident, noting a little soap had it looking as good as new. Other designer collaborations are discounted too, like this Scalamandré tiger-print piece and modern graphic style from Jonathan Adler, available in nine colorways.

Lulu & Georgia’s textured, high-pile, and solid color accent rugs come in rich shades of amber and green, with tufted 100% wool constructions that look and feel luxurious. More than a hundred products have been added to the sale section, like this editor-approved rug designed in partnership with Sarah Sherman Samuel (which you might recognize from Mandy Moore’s Altadena home). “Its contemporary look is neutral enough to align with lots of different aesthetics, whether you’re looking to add some whimsy to a midcentury decor scheme or bring some edge to a cottagecore setup,” shopping editor Audrey Lee shares in her review, adding that it hardly sheds. “The material has an elegant sheen to it that looks and feels almost like velvet, so it’s a dream to walk across, and it even brightens up the room a bit.” Another AD100 designer worth browsing is Jake Arnold, whose hand-loomed wool rug combines modern and traditional elements with tonal color-blocking and scalloped corners.

Known for its easy-care styles and collections sourced from design hubs like Morocco, India, and Turkey, direct-to-consumer brand Revival is one of our favorites when it comes to vintage and new rugs. Right now, you can get 15% off when you buy two rugs, with the offer extending to everything except for custom orders, rug pads, and swatches. If we could steer you toward two, we’d start with this washable vintage-inspired, lived-in rug, which fit right into the existing interiors of senior shopping editor Nashia Baker’s “moody midcentury” Brooklyn apartment. “I went with the ‘ruby’ option, which looks just as rich in person as it does online,” Baker says. “The floral details—my favorite feature—give the rug a modern romance that I don’t see as often in the market.” For something more understated, shopping producer Lauren Arzbaecher recommends the Mori Washable Wool Rug, calling it the “perfect neutral.” “The warm-toned stripes aren’t too loud, and play well against the brown velvet of my corner sectional,” she says, adding that it’s easy to clean and doesn’t shed as much as a typical wool rug.

The internet’s superstore has no shortage of quality transitional rugs for indoors and out, including celebrity-led and interior designer-backed collections. Joanna Gaines’ Magnolia Home collab with Loloi is on sale for a limited time, with deals on pieces like this indoor/outdoor striped rug in a versatile neutral palette. We’re also partial to Safavieh’s natural rug and the nuLOOM’s earthy tones and geometric patten.

We are always here for a Serena & Lily sale, and this year’s is no exception. Self-dubbed the Sale of the Year, its well curated, coastal vibes are up to 50% off across the site, including 30% off or more on all things floor coverings and free shipping on everything. We found great deals on natural fiber rugs and personality-packed picks like this charming floral number. We highly recommend a deep dive to find the piece that’s right for your vibe, whether that’s a vintage-inspired traditional rug, a breezy indigo blue design, or a hand-knotted wool option.

The Best Food Gifts Under $25 (That Feel Thoughtful and Chic)

📅 2025-11-06  |  Read Source →

Spoil them with a stoneware mugs, princess cake-inspired soap, and a charming Kewpie mayo ornament

If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Eater’s under-$25 holiday gift guide is, unabashedly, one of my favorites to curate during gift guide season — both as a shopping writer and a writer who lives, laughs, loves to shop. I live for the thrill of a thrifty find; that rush of finding the perfect gift that somehow comes in way under budget is a sensation I first experienced while thrifting with my mom as a kid, when I was taught to sniff out authentic English ironstone bowls like an Antiques Roadshow bloodhound. I have been John Wick-training for this moment.

The best gifts under $25 for the true food freaks in your life (including yourself) should speak to their specific culinary obsessions, tastebuds, and cult-fave restaurants. Keep an eye out for those limited-edition holiday gifts that are going to sell out soon, and, when you see a potential present, ask yourself: does it inspire whimsy? Why should I settle for a spoon rest that isn’t shaped like ravioli? Move those mugs and snacks from heritage and indie brands to the front of the line, and maybe even click add-to-cart twice so that you, too, can experience the magic of Spaghetti Dust.

Whether you’re looking for a White Elephant present or an offering to impress your in-laws, let’s shop for the best food- and drink-related gifts under $25.

Diaspora Spice Co. is one of my favorite places to buy spices online, because the selection is always exciting and the company pays its farm partners an average of six times more than the commodity price. This year’s enticingly versatile gingerbread spice blend caught my eye, because it can be used for baking, or for simply sprinkling over coffee for a festive boost. Bundle it up with a nice velvet bow and a highly specific, nostalgic thrift-store mug for a delightful gift.

The wonder elicited from this traveling tube of “Spaghetti Dust” — aka ready-to-sprinkle dried garlic, Calabrian chile flakes, parsley, and sea salt — with its groovy graphics and gift-ready packaging, makes it one of the coolest food-themed presents that’s sure to sell out this holiday season. Just add olive oil and al dente pasta, and you’re ready to eat a delicious meal.

There’s something so comforting about a stoneware mug — holding one makes me feel instantly more cozy and learned, like a Nancy Meyers character rediscovering joy in an English countryside cottage. The ceramic material makes stoneware a great insulator when it comes to heat retention (without burning your hands), and this rustic, splatter stoneware mug from Hudson Grace is a looker.

Your giftee has all the deep-cut Kewpie mayonnaise flavors. They might even own the Kewpie cookbook. Now, give them the gift of a Kewpie mayo ornament to solidify their fealty to the Japanese mayo brand.

Ya Albi is a Palestinian American, mother-daughter-owned company that sources its slightly sweet, full-bodied olive oil from the West Bank, and packages it all in a chic pink tin. Plus, all of the oil’s proceeds go toward HEAL Palestine, a nonprofit organization that supports Palestinian children impacted by the war on Gaza. (To shop for even more Palestinian olive oils, check out this Eater guide.)

Technically, it’s 20 cents over our $25 budget, but this princess cake-inspired soap from Flamingo Estate is too good to pass up. The soap is made by whipping together shea butter and raspberry oil, and perfumed with a combination of scents like sweet almond, heliotrope blossoms, and musky amber to create a marzipan and cream-esque olfactory profile. The bar is then given a final romantic garnish, and elegantly engraved with its prinsesstårta namesake.

Flamingo Estate Prinsesstårta Milk Bar Soap

From traditional, sprawling brasseries to the incoming wave of Parisian global gastronomy, Eater has you covered for dining out in the City of Lights with The Eater Guide to Paris. Whether your giftee is planning an upcoming trip to Paris or an aspirational one, this trusty tome is filled with vetted Eater favorites for every kind of hungry traveler.

It’s always a bonus when you find a gift with packaging so stunning that it’s already gift-ready. Pastiglie Leone is a heritage Italian confectionery whose candies make a perfect stocking stuffer, host gift, or present for the person in your life who owns a silver-plated toast rack and goes to high tea at least once a year.

For the home cook who also loves to journal, I suggest a fresh batch of snack-centric stickers. What better way is there to bookend a day than with a sticker spread featuring Pocky and Heineken beer?

This gift is great because it’s a present (novelty! whimsy!) and a hint about something quite practical (do the dishes!).

In the words of indie pantry brand Rooted Fare, this crunchy black sesame butter is “like if tang yuan and peanut butter had a baby.” Creamy and nutty, it’s the ideal spread for the friend with a semi-sweet tooth. I can’t stop eating it.

If someone you love loves to cook, it’s likely that they also love nice kitchen hand soaps and cleaning products. This non-toxic, bleach-free all-purpose cleaner from Avant has been in my Sunday cleaning prod rotation ever since I had my first whiff at the always chic Field and Fort in Summerland, California. The linen scent transports me to the smell of the clean laundry carts at Cité Internationale Universitaire in Paris, France, because it’s crisp, elegant, and subtle. I’ll use it to spot clean any surface, but I especially enjoy cleaning with it at the end of the day (or before hosting) on everything from kitchen sinks to table to surfaces. Bonus points for the fact that its refills come in little recyclable glass jars.

When designer Marta Cornwell invented this kale razor, she gave us the power to tame one of nature’s heartiest, most annoying versatile superfoods from the garden.

You never know what gems are hiding in the sale section of the MoMA Design Store. In this case: a set of four postmodern martini glasses. At nearly 60 percent off, this set delivers a chipper, serotonin-boosting jolt of color to the cocktail party that is welcome all year long, but especially in the frostier seasons.

MoMA Design Store Saturn Glassware Martini Glasses (Set of 4)

Weary spoons, whisks, and every other utensil under the Sun can find its throne upon this giant spoon rest shaped like ravioli. (As a perpetual splasher of sauce, the extra surface area is also appreciated.)

Ah, our patron saint of al fresco dining, roasted chicken, and “quarantinis”: the Barefoot Contessa herself. The handmade element of this Ina Garten ornament makes it perfect for your loved one’s shrine tree.

25 Great Gifts for New Dads, According to GQ

📅 2025-11-06  |  Read Source →

Becoming a dad changes a lot of things. Your sleep schedule, for one. Your relationship with a clean shirt, for another. But just because a guy has entered his daddy era doesn't mean he's stopped caring about the things he cared about before.

With that in mind, we've rounded up the best gifts for new dads, with a little something for him and the little one. Some are practical things that'll make those early days of fatherhood a little easier. Others are simply things that'll make him feel good, look good, and a little more like himself.

Nothing doing? Check out the rest of our gift guides and sign up for the GQ Recommends newsletter for more gift ideas worth your money.

At some point, he'll emerge back into the world, and there's nothing like a great shirt to ease the reentry. This swaggy checked shirt from Beams has all the layering built right in, so he can look like he hasn't missed a step.

There's a lot to be said for clothes that don't require much thought, especially when you've got a new bundle. Take this double-faced merino wool bomber from Quince: warm, unfussy, and easy to throw on with just about anything.

Some brands really are thinking of the children. Everybody.World makes its Trash Zip Hoodie from 100% recycled cotton waste, giving discarded material a second life as a very good sweatshirt.

A good pair of sweatpants is nonnegotiable. From the true masters of the category, these midweight terry sweatpants from Reigning Champ come with a relaxed silhouette, an open hem, and a nicely lived-in patina.

The undisputed king of dad shoes has entered its seventh generation, with its first major redesign since 2022 bringing a sleeker suede-and-mesh upper, softer cushioning, and all the Made in USA pedigree you'd expect. For a guy who's just become a dad, the timing couldn't be better.

He's a dad now. A man of refinement, responsibility, and a pressing need for a do-it-all boot. Enter Blundstone's new Heritage boot, a top-shelf take on its legendary shit-stomper, upgraded with premium leather and Goodyear-welted construction.

The baby's developing a sense of sight, and there's no reason for dad to sacrifice his. Lalo's Play Gym II is a far better-looking alternative to what's out there, with plenty to keep little hands and eyes occupied, including sensory toys, teethers, and a bell. The brand's set of high-contrast art cards wouldn't hurt, either.

If they've already got a Tripp Trapp, this one's a no-brainer. The iconic high chair is part of MoMA's permanent collection, and now the museum's Design Store has a set of colorful cushions to go with it.

One thing new parents can never have enough of is a good place to put the baby down. Part quilt, part playmat, these organic cotton numbers from House of Noa are among the most handsome we've seen, with an heirloom quality that makes 'em worth holding on to long after the baby has outgrown tummy time.

The problem with BabyBjörn? Too many good things to choose from. But for new parents, the gift of a few hands-free minutes is hard to beat. The new Bouncer Begin is designed specifically for newborns, with a shallower seat than the brand's wildly popular Bouncer Bliss.

Bottle-washing is a dad duty. We don't make the rules. Baby Brezza's Bottle Washer Pro 360 makes the job considerably less miserable, washing, sterilizing, and drying bottles in one go.

Two things you can never have enough of with a newborn: muslin and blankets. Coyuchi's wonderfully soft muslin quilt takes care of both.

New dads live by the clock. Three hours between feeds, 20 minutes until the next nap, two minutes to themselves, if they're lucky. Braun's Time Teacher, with its clean, easy-to-read dial, colorful hands, and markings for phrases like "quarter past" and "half past," makes keeping track a little easier. And when the little one is old enough to tell time, it'll come in handy all over again.

Apple's finally getting into the smart display game. The new HomeView is the company's first dedicated smart home hub, bringing home controls, FaceTime, and the usual Apple ecosystem conveniences to one ittle screen. Its 12-megapixel camera should come in especially handy for keeping the grandparents supplied with baby sightings.

A sleeping baby is a beautiful thing. Hatch's portable Go sound machine is a little godsend, with soothing sounds, a rechargeable battery, and a handy clip for attaching it to the stroller or car seat.

Bose's new sport-minded open earbuds let him enjoy his music or a podcast without tuning out what's happening around him—like, say, an actual human baby. And on the rare occasion he gets out for a run, they'll be just as useful for logging a few miles.

For the dad with his hands full (read: all dads), Ray-Ban's Meta Zena glasses pair a snazzy cat-eye silhouette with the ability to capture first steps, film stroller outings, or video-call the grandparents, all without reaching for his phone.

Tiny Vinyl's miniature record player and four-inch records are pure novelty, but there's something rather charming about a tiny turntable for a tiny human. Start building the little one's record collection now, and they'll have something to grow into.

7 Best Faux Garlands for Long-Lasting Holiday Cheer (2026)

With Halloween in the rearview, it’s time to take down the cobwebs and inflatable skulls and go full throttle into the holiday season. While seasonal garlands are fittingly festive, the natural editions tend to make a mess. For anyone who’d rather not be tasked with vacuuming the dead pine needles that seem to accumulate by the minute, faux garlands are a worthy solution. They offer the look (and often the feel) of the real thing without the sticky sap or endless cleanup.

Fake garlands have come a long way since their humble, low-quality beginnings. Now made with premium artificial foliage and durable wire frames, some of our favorites are nearly indistinguishable from their natural counterparts. Better yet, you can use them year after year to deck the halls (and mantels, bannisters, front porches… you get it), sometimes both indoors and out. No need to strip a tree of its limbs; simply light a pine-scented candle and let everyone think you did.

There’s not much more you could want in a garland than what this single, super-realistic-looking strand can accomplish. Afloral's bestselling Norfolk pine garland is eight feet long and more voluminous than many faux alternatives. Its branches and needles are intentionally spaced irregularly to give it a natural appearance, and the wired base makes it easy to shape, drape, and arrange just about anywhere. Wind it around a staircase or use it to dress up your front door; the possibilities are pretty much endless.

For those looking for a pre-arranged garland, we recommend Crate & Barrel’s Kew Garden garland by florist Abigail Ahern. A curated selection of faux evergreen fronds, berries, and twigs combines with velvet ribbons for an English-cottage-inspired centerpiece. The decoration work has been done for you; all you need to do now is hang it.

Simple but effective, the Fraser Fir is the kind of garland that practically begs to be draped over your mantel. Constructed with Balsam Hill’s proprietary True Needle foliage, the Fraser’s natural texture and full volume (read: no bare spots) make it look so convincingly real that your friends will wonder how you keep your home so tidy all season long. It’s available in multiple lengths (including the 10-foot strand for $159), with the option to add LED lights if you're after a little extra twinkle.

If traditional greenery isn't quite your thing, consider this garnet-hued strand as a fun alternative. Made of clusters of velvety, flocked bobbles, it adds rich color and plenty of texture to your seasonal setup. Weave it through a wreath or let it take center stage on its own. It's a little unexpected, which is sometimes exactly what a room needs.

If your priority in a faux garland is a natural-looking arrangement, consider this six-foot garland from McGee & Co., which has all the makings of a woodland find. Natural-looking pinecones and delicate, handcrafted white berries dot its lush, layered swaths of greenery, giving it plenty of intrigue without rendering it overly adorned. It's a lovely option for anyone who prefers their holiday decorations a little more rustic than glitzy.

This faux garland adds bright red berries and natural-looking pinecones to its lifelike pine greenery for an overall look that feels like it was gathered on a winter walk. At six feet long, it’s quite versatile, able to dress up a mantel or wind around a staircase. A plaid ribbon makes a nice finishing touch, if you're so inclined.

Who says Christmas decorations have to be red and green? This playful ball garland from CB2 takes a more eye-catching approach, combining warm metallic tones in a mix of sizes for plenty of visual interest. It's an apt design choice if you’re planning to go full tinsel mode this season, or simply looking to add a little shine to an otherwise understated setup.
